title: Gaussian elimination and echelon form
section: Gaussian Elimination ▷ Row Operations and Echelon Form
terms: coefficient matrix; augmented matrix; Gaussian elimination; elementary row operation; row equivalence; echelon form; pivot; back-substitution; reduced row echelon form.

exposition.text:
The augmented matrix [A | b] records a system Ax = b. Elementary row operations swap rows,
multiply a row by a nonzero scalar, or add a multiple of one row to another. Each preserves the
solution set and has an inverse operation. Gaussian elimination creates echelon form: nonzero
rows precede zero rows, and each leading nonzero entry lies to the right of the one above it.
These leading entries are pivots. Back-substitution solves from the bottom upward; columns
without pivots in the coefficient portion correspond to free variables. A row [0 · · · 0 | c] with
c ̸= 0 proves inconsistency. Reduced row echelon form additionally makes pivots 1 and the only
nonzero entries in their columns; it is unique although echelon forms need not be.
Row equivalent matrices have the same row space and the same reduced row echelon form;
having only the same rank is insufficient. A simultaneous set of row combinations preserves
every system precisely when its transformation is invertible. One must distinguish simultaneous
use of old rows from sequential elementary operations.

question.text:
For what value of a is x + y + z = 1, x + 2y + 3z = 2, 2x + 3y + az = 4 inconsistent?
(A) 2 (B) 3 (C) 4 (D) 5 (E) All real a

solution.text:
Subtract the first two equations from the third: (a − 4)z = 1. When a = 4 this is impossible.
For a ̸= 4, z is determined and the first two equations determine x, y uniquely.

question.text:
An augmented matrix has a row (0, 0, 0 | 2) after elimination. What follows?
(A) There is one free variable
(B) The homogeneous system is inconsistent
(C) There are two solutions
(D) The coefficient matrix is invertible
(E) The system is inconsistent

solution.text:
The row represents 0 = 2, which no choice of variables can satisfy. The corresponding ho-
mogeneous row would instead be 0 = 0 and would pose no inconsistency.

The original row space is the plane of vectors (s, 2s, t). In B both rows lie in it and are
independent: their coefficient pairs (2, 1) and (1, 1) have nonzero determinant. Hence their
reduced row echelon form is the original matrix. C has rank one; A, D, and E contain a
row outside that plane. Equal rank alone is not row equivalence.
